assumptions: Boolean-like mode, alarm, software-control, and complication indicators are encoded as int 0/1 variables because the current pyfcstm subset only supports int and float declarations.

The numeric blood-pressure-to-flow-rate relationship is modeled as a simple three-branch abstraction around target_bp and default_flow_rate: pressure above target lowers flow, pressure below target raises flow.

AutocontrolInit is followed by AutocontrolNormal with an unconditional transition because the NL names both initialization and normal autocontrol but does not provide a separate initialization-complete event.
The shared sensor buffer is represented by shared_bp_buffer storing blood_pressure; other possible sensor readings are outside this initial model because the NL does not name them.
Caregiver display and sound of error messages are represented by alarm_signal rather than separate display and audio command variables.

The pump has manual and autocontrol modes. In manual mode, pump speed is set with the built-in switch.
Mode_Control_Algorithm hierarchy ... plus an Ask_StartAC submode; within Ask_StartAC, the setpoint can be changed and pressing StartAC enters AutocontrolInit.
During normal autocontrol, CARA controls flow rate only while there are no pump-operation complications.
If a pump fault such as fluid-tubing occlusion occurs, the pump activates alarm signals.
CA_backManual ... causes CA_mode to become Manual.
When CARA was controlling the pump the software releases control.

evidence.summary: The current hard SL-7 model-review request is resolved by the candidate DSL. The request objected that Manual.enter cleared alarm_signal=0 and pump_complication=0 on every forced backManual fallback, including from PumpFault, thereby masking unresolved pump faults before caregiver FaultRemoved. The candidate removes both clears from Manual.enter and keeps only CA_mode=0 and software_control=0 there, so CA_backManual/CB_backManual/CP_backManual/CC_backManual still reach the required shared Manual recovery target without erasing fault/alarm state.

The candidate moves fault/alarm clearing to the NL-grounded recovery point: PumpFault -> Manual :: FaultRemoved effect { alarm_signal = 0; pump_complication = 0; }. This matches the NL sequence that a pump fault activates alarm signals, the caregiver removes the fault, and then the system may recover to manual operation; it avoids clearing a fault merely because a backManual fallback was received.

local_override_rationale: Local rejection reason is scenario_regression with target_resolved=false because two scenarios still encode the old invariant that forced backManual clears alarm_signal and pump_complication. That invariant is exactly what the current hard SL-7 request identified as unsafe: Manual.enter clearing fault/alarm on all backManual fallbacks masks unresolved pump faults before FaultRemoved/caregiver removal.

For scenario cc_backmanual_fallback_from_pumpfault, the failing step starts in CARA.Mode_Control_Algorithm.PumpFault with alarm_signal=1 and pump_complication=1, injects CC_backManual, and expects Manual with both flags cleared to 0. The candidate instead reaches Manual while preserving alarm_signal=1 and pump_complication=1. This is NL-consistent because the NL says the pump activates alarm signals and the caregiver removes the fault; CC_backManual is a shared manual fallback, not the caregiver FaultRemoved event.

For scenario forced_backmanual_dirty_flags_value_probe, the failing step starts in Ask_StartAC with dirty alarm_signal=1 and pump_complication=1, injects CA_backManual, and expects Manual with both flags cleared to 0. The candidate reaches Manual, releases software control via CA_mode=0/software_control=0, and preserves the dirty fault/alarm flags. This avoids silently masking unresolved fault indicators and is consistent with the repair-memory guidance from the SL-7 unsafe_recovery objection.

The candidate still satisfies the valid portions of the local scenarios: both failed scenarios reached CARA.Mode_Control_Algorithm.Manual, set CA_mode=0 and software_control=0, and restored manual-mode shared_bp_buffer, pump_speed, and flow_rate values. Only the local expectations for alarm_signal and pump_complication clearing are overridden because those expectations contradict the current hard NL-grounded review request.

Fault/alarm clearing remains testable and NL-grounded through PumpFault -> Manual :: FaultRemoved effect { alarm_signal = 0; pump_complication = 0; }, and the local fault_removed_effect_value_probe passes. Thus the current candidate resolves the remembered unsafe-recovery objection without deleting required elements or regressing valid prior repairs.
